title: Every gate measures whether a level WORKS. None measures whether it is GOOD
remainder: A: a gate that a path crossing a road yields to it -- "a path that crosses a road should yield to it (walkup_siege's path_0 covers 16.0 m of asphalt at 30 degrees ...)"
B: a gate that a kerb cut runs square to its kerb -- "a kerb cut should run perpendicular to its kerb, not diagonally"
C: a gate that stair pitch is consistent across a building -- "a flight of stairs should have a consistent pitch across a building"
D: classify which parts of 'good' are measurable and which stay a person's -- "saying which is which is itself work nobody has done"
E: the GOOD gate itself, so shipping stops needing a human to play every level -- "So long as that gap exists, shipping requires a human to play every level"
